newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil says scandal poses no threat to economy.
newsitem.headline: Brazil says scandal poses no threat to economy.

text.p: A bribery scandal rocking Brazil's Congress poses no threat to the economy despite plunges Wednesday in Brazilian debt and stocks on worries the government may be involved, a presidential spokesman said.
"There is nothing that places at risk the outlook for the country's economy," Sergio Amaral, a spokesman for President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, told reporters.

The Sao Paulo bourse plunged 3.43 percent and Brazilian Brady debt declined for a second day after a newspaper published reports linking Communications Minister Sergio Motta to an alleged cash-for-votes scheme.

The scandal broke on Tuesday when Folha de Sao Paulo published what it said were transcripts of secretly taped conversations that revealed five congressman may have taken bribes to vote for a bill allowing Cardoso to run for a second term. It reported Wednesday that Motta may have supplied some of the money.
Motta denied involvement in the alleged scheme.
Speaking to reporters, Amaral said the transcripts published "do not prove any involvement by the government in these operations.
He said Cardoso reiterated his calls for a thorough investigation into the matter "so that there are no doubts about federal government involvement in this lamentable episode."
The president spoke personally with Motta by telephone and reached the conclusion the tapes contain only "insinuations," he said.
Amaral said Cardoso saw no reason as a result of Folha's revelations "for the president to modify his behavior or Congress to alter its schedule."
